summary: This joint resolution blocks the EPA's April 2026 rule setting Renewable Fuel Standard volume requirements for 2026-2027 and waiving part of the 2025 cellulosic biofuel target by declaring the rule has no force or effect under the Congressional Review Act.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving an EPA rulemaking on renewable fuel standards. It contains no provisions related to federal spending levels, appropriations, or budget authority.
The legislation addresses only the validity of an EPA fuel-standard rule and has no tax provisions or revenue implications.
No connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical regulation appears in the bill text.
The resolution deals exclusively with environmental rulemaking and contains nothing related to firearms.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions are present.
The bill text is silent on reproductive health or abortion policy.
No defense or military spending language exists.

The joint resolution uses the Congressional Review Act to nullify an EPA rule that sets renewable fuel volume requirements and related standards under the Renewable Fuel Standard program. Because the RFS is an environmental regulation intended to promote lower-carbon fuels, disapproving the rule directly limits the scope or enforcement of federal environmental requirements in the fuels sector.
No welfare, entitlement, or social-services provisions are included.
The bill contains no education policy content.
No drug-enforcement or controlled-substance language appears.
The resolution does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
While renewable-fuel mandates can indirectly affect agricultural commodity markets, the bill itself makes no trade, tariff, or import-policy changes.
No deficit or debt-reduction measures are present.
The legislation is unrelated to LGBTQ legal protections.
No foreign-assistance provisions exist.
The bill addresses neither voting access nor election administration.
No technology, data, or privacy regulation content is included.
The resolution contains no labor or union-related provisions.
No religious-exemption or civil-rights provisions appear.
